articles.author: Xingliao Smart Home
articles.description:
Gateways are usually sold as coverage devices. The box promises to extend reach, blanket the property, and remove dead zones, which is a compelling pitch and mostly irrelevant to why the device is useful. A gateway is not a range extender, and treating it as one leads to buying it at the wrong moment and expecting the wrong result. What it actually does is quieter and more structural: it decides where decisions get made.
If your problem is that a camera at the far end of the property drops off the network, a gateway will not fix it. That is a radio problem between one device and one access point, and the fix is an access point, a better antenna, or a closer mounting position. Adding a gateway introduces a second network for some devices and leaves the original weak link exactly as weak as …
articles.title: A smart home gateway earns its place for three reasons, and none of them is range

Tiny footprint: About 900 KB in size.
Cross-platform: Runs on Windows (x64, ARM), macOS, Linux, Android, iOS/iPadOS, and WASM.

SSH UI Forwarding: Thanks to the JSON representation, you can easily pipe and forward the UI over SSH.
Polyglot examples: Comes with usage examples in Rust, C, C++, and even ASM.

articles.description:
App Attest and Play Integrity answer one question: is this my genuine app on a genuine device? That's worth knowing, and you should use them. But a real, unmodified app on a real phone passes, whether that phone is on a home connection or behind a proxy in a rack of phones.
So if you're fighting fake signups, bonus farming or account takeover, you need a second question: what network is this request coming from?
You can look for a VPN from inside the app. On Android, NetworkCapabilities.hasTransport(TRANSPORT_VPN) tells you about a VPN on the device. It's fine for showing a message, but it won't help against fraud, for two reasons:
The app is reporting on itself. A modified client can answer whatever it likes.
It can't see a proxy further upstream.
The check belongs on a server, which sees…
articles.title: App Attest and Play Integrity won't catch a real phone behind a proxy

articles.description:
Gamebreak is a new site of short browser puzzle games: open one between two tasks, finish in a few minutes, close it. No login wall, no account, no app install. It has around 70 games: Sudoku, Mahjong, FreeCell, 2048, a Tetris-style game, Hashi, Nonogram, Sokoban, a Wordle-style word game and more. Most rounds take 2–4 minutes.
The audience is office workers and students taking short breaks. That one decision drove almost every technical choice below.
Each game page is plain, hand-written HTML with a handful of script tags. On the 2048 page, for example, the page loads:
i18n.js – a tiny language helper (~3 KB)
score.js – the score store (~0.9 KB)
2048.js – the game itself (~6 KB)
share.js – result sharing
ads.js – ad slot setup
That's it. No bundler output, no hydration, no runtime framewo…

Hiring is one of the most honest signals a company gives off. A startup that suddenly opens six data-center engineering roles is building something big. In this tutorial we'll turn a plain list of eight companies into a single, clean table of open jobs. Th…
